## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.

| Swell size | Moderate | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |
| Swell period | Low | No sources found. |

| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 5 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> 11 sources: 10 read directly, plus SurferToday kept as web_search (403). 10 publishers. WIND remains weak and disputed. WannaSurf lists SE/E/NE as good wind (centred on E, 45 deg from 135). Surf Holidays says it works best with southwesterly winds (contradicts by 90 deg). RTE (2025) reports the usual westerly winds are too dangerous and that the wind switching southwest produced spectacular waves (an observation, so no value). No readable source explicitly confirms SE. The SE/S-SW statements on Surf-Forecast and Surf Atlas are about Mullaghmore Beach, not the Head, and were excluded. Swell direction: WannaSurf NW and W, Surf Holidays W to NW. Both overlap 285-320. Size: Surf Holidays 'starts breaking at about 10ft and can hold waves of up to 50ft and beyond', which matches the profile's 10-50 exactly (the profile may derive from it). WannaSurf says it starts at 12 ft+ and holds 16 ft and over (WannaSurf's top bin). Surf Atlas says it comes into its own over 15 ft swell and is best around 30-40 ft. Surfing-Waves says it easily holds over 20 ft. Record-day heights (49 ft in 2012 on Wikipedia, 60 ft from SurferToday) are not working ranges; SurferToday's unchanged 60 ft claim should not set the max. Tide: Surf Holidays high (it needs high tide to break out from the rock), WannaSurf mid and high, SurferToday (unread) high only. Consistent with mid_to_high, leaning high. Season: Surf Holidays late autumn and winter (Nov-Feb), Surf Atlas Dec-Mar, SurferToday (unread) Oct-Mar. All inside Oct-Mar. Period: no source gives a number, so the 14/17 s profile values are unverified. Bathymetry: GSI (official, 2004) describes the Head as a rock platform of Carboniferous sandstone, siltstone and shale; this is land and foreshore geology, not a survey of the reef. WannaSurf says flat rocks; Surf Atlas a barnacle-covered rock ledge; Surf Holidays a ledge of reef. Location: about 400-500 m NW/N of the village (Wikipedia, Surf Atlas). No peer-reviewed study of the break was found on Crossref.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 10 ft [S6] · 12 ft [S4] | conflicting | S4, S6 | `wave_height_min_ft` 10 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 30–40 ft | documented | S7 | no separate setting; working range 10–50 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 50 ft and beyond (no upper limit stated) | documented | S4, S6, S7, S9 | `wave_height_max_ft` 50 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: Surf Holidays says it starts breaking at about 10 ft and WannaSurf says it starts working at over 3.5 m / 12 ft; neither says whether this is face or offshore swell height.
  - S6 (Surf Holidays): “Mullaghmore starts breaking at about 10ft and can hold waves of up to 50ft and beyond.”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at Over 3.5m / 12ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
- **Ideal range**: The Surf Atlas says it tends to be at its best around the 30-40 ft range (scale not stated) and comes into its own when the swell peaks over 15 ft (stated as swell).
  - S7 (The Surf Atlas): “Mullaghmore can hold anything really but tends to be at its monstrous best around the 30-40 foot range”
  - S7 (The Surf Atlas): “comes into its own when the swell peaks over 15 feet”
- **Maximum suitable**: Surf Holidays says it can hold waves of up to 50 ft and beyond, the Surf Atlas says it can hold anything, Surfing-Waves says it holds over 20 ft and stays surfable in the biggest Atlantic swells, and WannaSurf's top bracket (16 ft and over) is open-ended; scales are not stated.
  - S6 (Surf Holidays): “Mullaghmore starts breaking at about 10ft and can hold waves of up to 50ft and beyond.”
  - S7 (The Surf Atlas): “Mullaghmore can hold anything really but tends to be at its monstrous best around the 30-40 foot range”
  - S9 (Surfing-Waves): “this spot can easily hold waves in excess of 20 feet and remains surfable in the biggest swells the Atlantic has to offer”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at Over 3.5m / 12ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: Surf Holidays says it starts breaking at about 10 ft and WannaSurf says it starts working at over 3.5 m / 12 ft; neither says whether this is face or offshore swell height.
- **Wind · offshore**: WannaSurf lists southeast, east and northeast as good winds, while Surf Holidays says it works best with south-westerly winds; RTE (2025) reports one day on which the wind switching southwest gave spectacular waves (an observation, not a stated offshore direction).
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf Holidays calls it a high-tide spot and SurferToday (search summary) says it can only be surfed at high tide, while WannaSurf gives mid and high tide.
